high.title: Economists Raise 2026 Inflation Again; See Monday's Focus (11)
high.summary: Economists surveyed by the Central Bank adjusted inflation projections for the ninth consecutive time according to the Focus Bulletin. IPCA expectations for 2026 rose from 4.89% to 4.91%, above the Central Bank's tolerance range for the inflation target. For 2027-2029, estimates remained at 4%, 3.64%, and 3.50% respectively. Selic rate forecasts held at 13% for this year but rose to 11.25% for 2027, staying at 10% for 2028-2029. USD/BRL is expected at R$ 5.20 by year-end, with projections of R$ 5.30, R$ 5.35, and R$ 5.40 for 2027-2029. This persistent inflation overshoot signals continued hawkish Central Bank stance and prolonged high real rates, supporting BRL but weighing on equities. The sticky inflation above target despite tight monetary policy suggests structural pressures that could delay the easing cycle, keeping Brazilian assets in a high-carry environment.

high.title: April IPCA Rises 0.67% and Accumulates 4.39% Increase, Within Expectations
high.summary: Brazil's official inflation accelerated with IPCA rising 0.67% in April, matching market expectations exactly. The 12-month accumulated inflation reached 4.39%, still within the Central Bank's tolerance range of 3% ±1.5pp but approaching the upper limit. This compares to 0.88% in March and 0.43% in April 2025. Food and beverages led the increase with 1.34% monthly rise, contributing 0.29pp to the index, followed by health and personal care. The result confirms inflation persistence near the tolerance ceiling, supporting the Central Bank's hawkish stance and high Selic rates. With inflation expectations consistently above target in the Focus survey, this data reinforces market views that aggressive monetary tightening will continue, benefiting BRL carry trades while pressuring interest-sensitive sectors. Bond yields likely to remain elevated as real rates stay restrictive.

high.title: Market Reacts to Petrobras' R$ 9 Billion JCP and IPCA; Ibovespa in Dollars Falls
high.summary: Brazilian markets are digesting Petrobras' Q1 2026 results showing net profit of R$ 32.7 billion, down 7.2% year-over-year. The company approved R$ 9 billion in shareholder remuneration (R$ 0.70 per share) as an advance on 2026 payments, to be distributed in two equal tranches via interest on equity (JCP) in August and September. Ex-dividend date is June 2nd. The substantial dividend payout supports Petrobras as a defensive play amid market volatility, though the profit decline reflects challenging operational conditions. Combined with today's IPCA release showing inflation at 4.39% (near target ceiling), markets face mixed signals. High oil prices from Middle East conflict support Petrobras fundamentals while persistent inflation reinforces Central Bank hawkishness, benefiting BRL but creating headwinds for broader equity valuations.

medium.title: Compass Debuts Today on B3, First IPO in Five Years; Analyst Sees Up to 57% Potential from Start
medium.summary: Compass (PASS3), Cosan's gas distribution unit, breaks Brazil's four-year IPO drought with its B3 debut. The company priced at R$ 28 (bottom of range), raising R$ 3.2 billion and achieving R$ 20 billion valuation. EQI analysts set price target of R$ 42-44, implying up to 57% upside potential. The bottom-range pricing reflects weak market conditions amid Middle East war uncertainties but may create opportunities for investors in this established, solid company.

medium.title: Itaúsa (ITSA4), Petrobras (PETR4), Raízen (RAIZ4) and Other Highlights This Tuesday (12)
medium.summary: Itaúsa (ITSA4) reported Q1 2026 recurring net profit of R$ 4.49 billion, up 17% year-over-year, with ROE reaching 20.1% vs 17.4% previously. Results were driven by Itaú Unibanco's 11% improvement and 76% surge in non-financial investments. Administrative expenses rose 10.8% to R$ 44 million. The strong performance reflects the resilience of Brazil's banking sector amid high interest rate environment.

medium.title: Petrobras (PETR4): Company ADRs Oscillate in New York Despite R$ 9 Billion JCP and Oil Price Rise
medium.summary: Petrobras ADRs trade mixed in NY pre-market despite announcing R$ 9 billion JCP payment and rising oil prices from Middle East conflict. PBR fell 0.24% to $20.70 while PBRa gained 0.11% to $18.95. Brent crude surged 3.55% to $107.89 and WTI rose 3.79% to $101.80. Q1 net profit was R$ 32.7 billion, down 7.2% year-over-year, with revenues of R$ 123.7 billion.
